name: Rear Calipers
description: ZL1 / ZL1 1LE (J6G): Brembo 4-piston fixed rear calipers (2x32, 2x28 mm) bolted directly to the rear knuckle, 365 x 28 mm one-piece rotors. Base/SS non-1LE (JL9/J55): single-piston floating caliper on a bracket. Race: AP Radi-CAL 4-piston (Essex rear kit) retaining the OEM drum-in-hat park brake.

components.name: Rear brake caliper
components.description: Rear calipers do ~30–35% of the braking. On ZL1 the rear 4-piston fixed caliper works with a drum-in-hat park brake inside the rotor hat (cable puller, RPO J77) – the caliper itself has no park-brake motor.
components.location: Rear knuckle, approx center x≈2.97, y≈0.37, z≈±0.71 (position approximate – trailing placement assumed; verify on your knuckle).

factory.name: Brembo 4-piston fixed rear caliper, ZL1 / ZL1 1LE (J6G)
factory.notes: Pistons 2x32, 2x28 mm; 365x28 mm rotor. SS 1LE also uses 4-piston rears. GM offered a rear 4-piston kit for SS without 1LE.

raceOptions.name: AP Racing by Essex Radi-CAL Competition rear kit, 365x30 mm
raceOptions.partNumber: Caliper CP9449 (listed by retailer) – another retailer lists CP9450-2/3S4L; confirm with Essex
raceOptions.notes: Retains OEM parking brake; saves ~6 lb unsprung vs OEM rear.

raceOptions.name: Wilwood / StopTech rear kits for Gen 6

hardware.torqueSequence: Single pass 125 N·m (some owners report an additional 15–30° – verify in GM SI)
hardware.threadlocker: Blue threadlocker on ~2/3 of thread length (owner-reported procedure)
hardware.notes: GM 2016–18 table "Rear brake caliper bolt 125 N·m J6G". [2026-10 check] The same camaro6.com SI quote gives rear caliper bolts 125 N·m (92 lb ft) [2x] with no angle step, which matches TightTorque. Not in a GM primary document; stays typical.

hardware.item: Base/SS (JL9/J55) rear caliper bracket bolt – reference only
hardware.torqueSequence: First pass 100 N·m, then final angle per GM SI

hardware.item: Base/SS rear caliper guide pin bolt – reference only

hardware.notes: GM lists 11 N·m (JL9/J55 rear). Brembo J6G rear bleeder assumed similar – verify.

installNotes: Install park-brake shoes and rotor first.
Bleeders up; torque bolts with threadlocker.
Bleed order: RR, LR, RF, LF; inner bleeder then outer on each caliper.
inspection: As front; rear pads usually last 2–3x the fronts.
